      "startEvent": 677,
      "endEvent": 690,
      "contextStartEvent": 548,
      "contextEndEvent": 690,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "Still, none of these can impeach the idea that we did it not too soon, but much too late",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The closing affirmation expressly discounts the preceding failures and blunders as objections to intervention's timing. However, B supplies legal and strategic reasons at E569–677 and may be distinguishing implementation from justification. It is unclear whether all consequential objections are excluded regardless of merit; the affirmation does not simply replace absent reasons."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 780,
      "endEvent": 782,
      "contextStartEvent": 753,
      "contextEndEvent": 805,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "Who but a slave desires such a ghastly fate?",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame",
        "fear"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B associates wanting the described afterlife with servility, potentially discrediting someone who welcomes it. But E766–778 supplies the surveillance-and-punishment argument, and the question is bounded by that description. The text does not clearly establish that objections to the description itself would also count as servility."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 922,
      "endEvent": 929,
      "contextStartEvent": 877,
      "contextEndEvent": 930,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "they convict themselves of being first very stupid and second very immoral.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame",
        "ridicule"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "After arguing from prolonged suffering and delayed revelation at E893–921, B makes accepting the described account itself evidence of intellectual and moral defect. That protects his conclusion against an adherent's disagreement by discrediting the adherent. The protection is scoped to this account; the surrounding argument supplies reasons and is not a slogan."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1284,
      "endEvent": 1287,
      "contextStartEvent": 1246,
      "contextEndEvent": 1288,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "These points cannot be overthrown by any kind of casuistry",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "ridicule"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B declares his design objections immune to 'casuistry' and applies that label to A's earlier response. E1248–1283 supplies the actual cosmological and moral argument. The wording could pre-dismiss future answers, but it could also exclude only reasoning B regards as specious; unrestricted protection against substantive objections is not established."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1672,
      "endEvent": 1683,
      "contextStartEvent": 1562,
      "contextEndEvent": 1691,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "You may borrow with pleasure uh the morality of the religious if you wish to do so",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame",
        "identity"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The borrowing affirmation classifies unbelievers' morality as religious property without establishing that exclusivity here. A previously argues for transcendent authority at E1008–1157, while B offers solidarity at E1577–1652. Whether this is unsupported substitution or a compressed disputed premise remains uncertain; calling denial an untruth suggests, but does not establish, blanket protection."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2088,
      "endEvent": 2093,
      "contextStartEvent": 2071,
      "contextEndEvent": 2120,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "Nor has he, nor has you, nor have you. Nobody has. We don't know.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "A moves from personal ignorance to universal ignorance to support reopening the origins question. E2074–2087 discusses book availability, not why relevant scientific knowledge is absent; E2094–2120 concerns suppression and hostility. The universal affirmation supplies that missing bridge, although his invitation to discussion leaves blanket exclusion of evidence uncertain."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2115,
      "endEvent": 2120,
      "contextStartEvent": 2071,
      "contextEndEvent": 2177,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "which actually makes me wonder whether the ID people may not have a point.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "A treats opponents' alleged intolerance as a reason to suspect merit in intelligent design, potentially turning criticism into confirmation. Yet E2115–2120 specifies hostility toward qualified skepticism and expresses only tentative suspicion. This is an ordinary, contestable inference about conduct; it does not clearly make every substantive objection confirm the view."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2396,
      "endEvent": 2415,
      "contextStartEvent": 2303,
      "contextEndEvent": 2459,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "and then we'll be on a level playing field.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "identity"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B restricts a fair counterexample to societies explicitly adopting his named rationalist tradition, potentially excluding atheist dictatorships by definition. However, E2305–2312 concedes atheists can be murderous, and E2371–2395 offers a religious-inheritance explanation. The test may distinguish rational humanism from mere atheism rather than immunize atheism against all contrary evidence."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2536,
      "endEvent": 2544,
      "contextStartEvent": 2465,
      "contextEndEvent": 2583,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "You for this question to be valid at all must propose and point out a government",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "identity",
        "ridicule"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "After A cites Soviet anti-religious persecution at E2481–2513, B makes the objection's validity depend on identifying a government adopting his preferred thinkers. This expressly excludes the offered evidence from that challenge. E2514–2535 supplies a rival historical explanation, and E2572–2575 narrows the defended values; this is protected argument, not a slogan."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2661,
      "endEvent": 2676,
      "contextStartEvent": 2609,
      "contextEndEvent": 2689,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "Totalitarian first in their origin, genocidal in their conclusions.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "fear"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B extends the preceding account of particular apocalyptic factions to 'all religions' at E2662 and then to religion poisoning everything at E2675–2676. Earlier arguments explain objections to religious authority, but do not establish universal genocidal conclusions. E2677–2689 returns to specified congregations, limiting the final warning without earning the intervening universal claim."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 2247,
      "endEvent": 2259,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "the idea that either side is faultless in this is absurd and indefensible.",
      "explanation": "A explicitly acknowledges human wickedness and dangerous religious misunderstanding, rejecting immunity for either side. This qualification matters when interpreting his earlier claims about religion and morality; he renews the concession at E2465–2467."

      "startEvent": 1713,

      "quote": "meant one had to change one's own opinion or analysis one would be um obliged to do so",
